'''Giulio Casati''' (born December 10, 1942) is Emeritus Professor of Theoretical Physics at [[University of Insubria]]. Casati is known for his work on [[chaos theory|chaos]], both classical and [[Quantum chaos|quantum]], being considered one of the pioneers of the latter.
Casati is in fact principally known for the discovery of quantum dynamical localization phenomenon, that highlighted the relevance of chaos in quantum mechanics. His landmark paper, with Boris Chirikov, Joseph Ford and Felix Izrailev,<ref>{{cite book | last1=Casati | first1=G. | last2=Chirikov | first2=B. V. | last3=Izraelev | first3=F. M. | last4=Ford | first4=Joseph | title=Stochastic Behavior in Classical and Quantum Hamiltonian Systems | chapter=Stochastic behavior of a quantum pendulum under a periodic perturbation | publisher=Springer-Verlag | location=Berlin/Heidelberg | isbn=3-540-09120-3 | doi=10.1007/bfb0021757 | pages=334–352|volume=93|year=1979|series=Lecture notes in Physics}}</ref> is among the most quoted in the field. With Boris Chirikov, Italo Guarneri and Dima Shepelyansky Casati also discovered that quantum localization deeply affects the excitation of hydrogen atom in strong monochromatic fields.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Casati | first1=Giulio | last2=Chirikov | first2=B. V. | last3=Shepelyansky | first3=D. L. | title=Quantum Limitations for Chaotic Excitation of the Hydrogen Atom in a Monochromatic Field | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=53 | issue=27 | date=1984-12-31 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.53.2525 | pages=2525–2528| bibcode=1984PhRvL..53.2525C }}</ref> Further major contributions considered the connections between quantization of non integrable systems and the statistical theory of spectra.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Casati | first1=G. | last2=Valz-Gris | first2=F. | last3=Guarnieri | first3=I. | title=On the connection between quantization of nonintegrable systems and statistical theory of spectra | journal=Lettere al Nuovo Cimento | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=28 | issue=8 | year=1980 | issn=1827-613X | doi=10.1007/bf02798790 | pages=279–282| s2cid=120010808 }}</ref> With the advent of quantum computing Casati and his coworkers studied the efficient quantum computing of complex dynamics.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Benenti | first1=Giuliano | last2=Casati | first2=Giulio | title=Quantum computers: where do we stand? | journal=Europhysics News | publisher=EDP Sciences | volume=36 | issue=1 | year=2005 | issn=0531-7479 | doi=10.1051/epn:2005105 | pages=16–20| doi-access=free | bibcode=2005ENews..36...16B }}</ref><ref>G. Benenti, G. Casati and G. Strini, Principles of quantum computation and information, Volume I: Basic concepts (World Scientific, Singapore, 2004).</ref><ref>G. Benenti, G. Casati and G. Strini, Principles of quantum computation and information, Volume II: Basic tools and special topics (World Scientific, Singapore, 2007).</ref><ref>G. Casati, D.L. Shepelyansky, P. Zoller and G. Benenti (Eds.), Quantum computers, algorithms and chaos, Proceedings of the ''E. Fermi'' Varenna School, Course CLXII, Varenna, Italy, 5–15 July 2005 (IOS Press and SIF, Bologna, 2006)</ref> 
On the classical side, Casati's interests regarded mostly energy conduction in non-linear lattices:<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Terraneo | first1=M. | last2=Peyrard | first2=M. | last3=Casati | first3=G. | title=Controlling the Energy Flow in Nonlinear Lattices: A Model for a Thermal Rectifier | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=88 | issue=9 | date=2002-02-14 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.88.094302 | article-number=094302| pmid=11864013 | arxiv=cond-mat/0201125 | bibcode=2002PhRvL..88i4302T | s2cid=119407302 }}</ref> from the earliest numerical proof of the validity of Fourier law in one-dimensional many body systems, obtained in collaboration with Bill Wisscher, Franco Vivaldi, and Joseph Ford,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Casati | first1=Giulio | last2=Ford | first2=Joseph | last3=Vivaldi | first3=Franco | last4=Visscher | first4=William M. | title=One-Dimensional Classical Many-Body System Having a Normal Thermal Conductivity | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=52 | issue=21 | date=1984-05-21 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.52.1861 | pages=1861–1864| bibcode=1984PhRvL..52.1861C }}</ref> to the description of a thermal rectifier and of a thermal transistor.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Li | first1=Baowen | last2=Wang | first2=Lei | last3=Casati | first3=Giulio | title=Negative differential thermal resistance and thermal transistor | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=88 | issue=14 | date=2006-04-03 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.2191730 |arxiv=cond-mat/0410172 | page=143501| bibcode=2006ApPhL..88n3501L | hdl=11383/1501461 | s2cid=118962955 | url=http://scitation.aip.org/content/aip/journal/apl/browse | hdl-access=free }}</ref> The same techniques lead to the theoretical demonstration of a one-way mirror for light<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Lepri | first1=Stefano | last2=Casati | first2=Giulio | title=Asymmetric Wave Propagation in Nonlinear Systems | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=106 | issue=16 | date=2011-04-18 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.106.164101 | article-number=164101| pmid=21599368 | arxiv=1103.4802 | bibcode=2011PhRvL.106p4101L | s2cid=9455492 }}</ref>

Casati has received the Italian Prize for Physics "F. Somaini" (1991),<ref>{{cite web|title=Premio Somaini|url=http://www.centrovolta.it/volta/download/Premio_%20Somaini.doc|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220618133001/http://www.centrovolta.it/volta/download/Premio_%20Somaini.doc|archive-date=June 18, 2022}}</ref> the [[Enrico Fermi Prize]] (2008)<ref>{{cite web|title=premio Fermi |url=http://www.sif.it/attivita/premio_fermi |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110160831/http://www.sif.it/attivita/premio_fermi |archive-date=2014-11-10 }}</ref>(the most important Italian prize for Physics), the Premio internazionale per la fisica della Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei (2010),<ref>{{cite web|title=Accademia dei Lincei|url=http://www.lincei.it/index.php}}</ref> the Sigillo Longobardo (2010).<ref>{{cite web|title=Sigillo Longobardo|url=http://archivio.agi.it/articolo/781bf98ae12197f8d9045d8ab9313be0_20101021_lombardia-festa-statuto-tra-premiati-mogol-e-monsignor-padovese}}</ref> He is a Member of the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Casati Giulio |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Casati_Giulio |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref> and the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Academia Europaea|url=http://www.euro-acad.eu/members?utf8=%E2%9C%93&land=Italy&klass=4&filter=&sort=&way}}</ref> and is the author/coauthor of over 300 publications.<ref>{{cite web|title=Researchgate|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Giulio_Casati}}</ref>

Casati received his MS from the [[University of Milan]] in 1968,  and from 1968 to 1971 was a Postdoctoral fellow at CCR Euratom – Ispra (Italy). In 1971-1972 he visited [[Georgia Tech|Georgia Institute of Technology]] as Research associate. He was then appointed Associate professor at the University of Milan 1973–1987, being appointed full professor of Theoretical Physics at the University of Milan in 1987. From 1993 to 1998 he also served as vice Dean of School of Science and Technology in the University of Milan. He then supervised the creation of a new university in Como, where he was Adjunct to the Rector from 1998 to 2001. Since 2002 he has also been on the faculty of the [[National University of Singapore]].<ref>{{cite web|title=National University of Singapore|url=http://www.quantumlah.org/people/casati}}</ref> In 2014 he officially retired from the University of Insubria. Presently, he is also distinguished professor at the [[International Institute of Physics (IIP)|International Institute of Physics]] of the Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil.<ref>{{cite web|title=International Institute of Physics|url=http://www.iip.ufrn.br/researchers}}</ref>
Casati worked much to develop the scientific activities in his hometown of Como, where he founded the Centro di Cultura Scientifica Alessandro Volta,<ref>{{cite web|title=Fondazione Alessandro Volta|url=http://www.centrovolta.it/volta|access-date=2016-07-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160731091949/http://www.centrovolta.it/volta/|archive-date=2016-07-31}}</ref> a world-renokwn Conference Center. 
He is presently the scientific director of the Lake Como School of Advanced Studies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lake Como School of Advanced Studies|url=http://lakecomoschool.org/about/governing-bodies|website=Lake Como School}}</ref>
He also founded the Center for Non-linear and Complex Systems at the University of Insubria, which he directed until 2014, when he was nominated honorary president<ref>{{cite web|title=Center for Nonlinear and Complex Systems|url=http://www.dfm.uninsubria.it/complex/|access-date=2014-08-23|archive-date=2014-09-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924142014/http://www.dfm.uninsubria.it/complex/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
